answer: Each identity locks 60 credits in a vault bond and posts one claim at the wharf registry, backed by a key-bound work record. Any peer may stake 10 to challenge a claim; the auditor rechecks it, and a hollow claim with no work burns the 60 bond and voids that payout, while a false challenge loses the 10. The filing fee is 15 per claim, so the k-th fake costs 75; 1,000 fakes cost 75,000. A rented-work ring fails because rented records carry their owner's key and cannot match a second claimant. An honest agent locks one bond, posts one true claim, and recovers it after close, losing only 15.
